title: Descent of the category of finitely presented algebraic spaces over affine limits
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is finitely presented if it is quasi-compact, quasi-separated (its diagonal is quasi-compact), and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, let $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of affine schemes with affine transition maps, and let $T=\varprojlim_i T_i$. For an affine scheme $U$ let $\mathsf{FP}(U)$ have finitely presented algebraic spaces over $U$ as objects and all $U$-morphisms as arrows. Base change defines the transition functors. The canonical functor $2\!\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}\mathsf{FP}(T_i)\to\mathsf{FP}(T)$ is an equivalence. Explicitly, every finitely presented algebraic space over $T$ is isomorphic to $Y_i\times_{T_i}T$ for some $Y_i\in\mathsf{FP}(T_i)$; for $Y_i,Z_i\in\mathsf{FP}(T_i)$, every $T$-morphism between their pullbacks is the pullback of a morphism at some $j\ge i$; and two stage morphisms whose pullbacks to $T$ agree become equal at a sufficiently late common stage. Fibre products are those of [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 07SK (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), specialized to affine scheme bases; base change of finite presentation: spaces-morphisms.tex, Tag 03XR (lemma-base-change-finite-presentation).

proof.text: Base change preserves finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], so all transition and comparison functors in the statement are defined. Let $Y\to T$ be finitely presented. Apply [lem-sfb-fp-etale-presentation-criterion] to choose an affine etale presentation $q:W\to Y$ with $W$ and its scheme kernel pair $R=W\times_YW$ both finitely presented over $T$. Write $s,t:R\rightrightarrows W$ for the projections. By [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation], $(s,t):R\to W\times_TW$ is an etale equivalence relation and the canonical map from the fppf sheaf quotient $W/R$ to $Y$ is an isomorphism identifying the quotient map with $q$.

source.place: Tag 07SK (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), first paragraph, with base-change stability from Tag 03XR

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to the two schemes $W,R$ over $T$. Directedness gives a common stage $i$ with finitely presented models $W_i,R_i$ over $T_i$; moving the models to this stage preserves finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Clause (2) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] then descends both $s,t$ to $s_i,t_i:R_i\rightrightarrows W_i$ after enlarging $i$. Every stage base is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, as required in that theorem. The same permanence node, (2), makes $W_i,R_i$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. All comparisons with $W,R$ are the base-change identifications supplied by that theorem.

source.place: Tag 07SK, first paragraph: descent of W, R and the two projections, using Tag 01ZM

proof.text: We record explicitly the local finite-presentation checks needed for the next step. Any map between schemes finitely presented over an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally finitely presented: on affine source and target opens its algebra map has the form $C\to B$ with $C=A[y_1,\ldots,y_m]/J$ and $B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/K$, with $J,K$ finitely generated, by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. If $y_a$ maps to $p_a(x)$, then $B=C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(K(x),y_a-p_a(x))$, a finite presentation by [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]; applying the pointwise definition [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] proves the assertion. The same presentations show local finite type by forgetting the relations. Products over the affine base are finitely presented: a projection is a base change, and the structure map is its composite with the other structure map, by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3) and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](d). In particular this applies to $s_i,t_i$ and $j_i=(s_i,t_i):R_i\to W_i\times_{T_i}W_i$, and all their source and target schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

source.place: Tags 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), 02FV (lemma-finite-presentation-permanence); the displayed finite-algebra presentation is written out here

proof.text: The limiting maps $s,t$ are etale, and $j=(s,t):R\to W\times_TW$ is a monomorphism because $R$ is the kernel pair of $W\to Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-descend-etale], applied separately to $s_i,t_i$, and [lem-weil-pbc-descend-monomorphism], applied to $j_i$, a common later stage has $s_i,t_i$ etale and $j_i$ a monomorphism. Etaleness persists under further base change by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]; a pullback of a monomorphism is a monomorphism because equality of its two projected arrows forces equality by the fibre-product universal property. Thus a common stage and all subsequent enlargements retain these properties. Their hypotheses hold by the preceding step: the stage base and the source and target schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the first two maps are locally finitely presented, and $j_i$ is locally of finite type. We use base-change models throughout as required by both descent lemmas.

source.place: Tag 07SK, first paragraph: eventual etaleness and monomorphism, using Tags 07RP and 07RQ

proof.text: It remains to ensure an equivalence relation, rather than only an etale monomorphism. At the limit the kernel pair has maps $e:W\to R$, $v:R\to R$ and $c:P=R\times_{t,W,s}R\to R$, given by $w\mapsto(w,w)$, $(w_1,w_2)\mapsto(w_2,w_1)$ and $((w_1,w_2),(w_2,w_3))\mapsto(w_1,w_3)$. The scheme $P_i=R_i\times_{t_i,W_i,s_i}R_i$ is finitely presented over $T_i$: the preceding finite-algebra calculation makes $s_i,t_i$ locally finitely presented; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes them quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and its (3) and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](d) apply to the product. Clause (2) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] descends $e,v,c$ to a common later stage. Clause (3), applied finitely many times, makes the six equations $s_ie_i=t_ie_i=\mathrm{id}$, $s_iv_i=t_i$, $t_iv_i=s_i$, $s_ic_i=s_i\operatorname{pr}_1$, $t_ic_i=t_i\operatorname{pr}_2$ hold there. On points of every $T_i$-scheme these equations give reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity, respectively. Together with the monomorphism $j_i$, they make $R_i\rightrightarrows W_i$ an etale equivalence relation. No groupoid-axiom assertion is inferred merely from the existence of $s_i,t_i$.

source.place: Tag 07SK, first paragraph, expanded relation-axiom descent before setting Y_i=W_i/R_i; Tag 01ZM(2),(3)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] over $T_i$ to obtain the algebraic space $Y_i=W_i/R_i$ and its etale surjective atlas with kernel pair $R_i$. By [lem-sfb-fp-etale-presentation-criterion], $Y_i\to T_i$ is finitely presented, since $W_i,R_i$ are. Pull the atlas back to $T$. It is still an etale surjective atlas, with kernel pair the pullback of $R_i$, by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its presentation is exactly $R\rightrightarrows W$. By [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation], applied to the atlases $W\to Y$ and $W\to Y_i\times_{T_i}T$, both spaces are the sheaf quotient $W/R$ compatibly with the maps from $W$. The quotient universal property of [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] gives maps $Y_i\times_{T_i}T\to Y$ and $Y\to Y_i\times_{T_i}T$, each induced by the identity on $W$ and respecting its two maps from $R$. Each composite restricts to the identity on $W$, so uniqueness of quotient factorization makes both composites identities. These maps are over $T$, since their structure maps also agree on $W$. Thus the comparison is an isomorphism over $T$, proving essential surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 07SK, conclusion of its first paragraph; quotient Tag 02WW

proof.text: Fix $i$ and finitely presented $Y_i,Z_i$ over $T_i$, and a $T$-map $\alpha:Y\to Z$ between their pullbacks. By [lem-sfb-fp-etale-presentation-criterion], choose an affine etale surjective $W_i\to Y_i$ with $R_i=W_i\times_{Y_i}W_i$ finitely presented over $T_i$. For $j\ge i$ put $W_j=W_i\times_{T_i}T_j$ and $R_j=R_i\times_{T_i}T_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit] these are affine-transition systems with limits $W$ and $R$; their stages are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. The pullback atlases and kernel pairs are those of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Apply [lem-sfb-lfp-space-scheme-limit-test] with fixed base $T_i$ and fixed target $Z_i$, which is locally finitely presented over $T_i$. The composite $W\to Y\xrightarrow{\alpha}Z\to Z_i$ is a $T_i$-map and hence comes from $b_j:W_j\to Z_i$ for some $j\ge i$.

source.place: Tag 07SK, second paragraph: descend the map on an affine atlas, using Tags 04AK and 0CP4

proof.text: The two maps $b_j s_j,b_j t_j:R_j\to Z_i$ agree after pullback to $R$, because the limiting map factors through $Y$. The injectivity part of [lem-sfb-lfp-space-scheme-limit-test], now on the quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme system $(R_k)_{k\ge j}$, makes them equal at some later $k$. Pair $b_k$ with $W_k\to T_k$ to obtain a $T_k$-map $W_k\to Z_k=Z_i\times_{T_i}T_k$. It equalizes the two maps from $R_k$. Since $R_k$ is the kernel pair of the base-changed atlas $W_k\to Y_k$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation] identifies $Y_k$ with the sheaf quotient $W_k/R_k$, so the universal property in [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] gives a unique sheaf map $\alpha_k:Y_k\to Z_k$. It is over $T_k$: its composite to $T_k$ and the structure map of $Y_k$ agree on $W_k$, hence agree by the same uniqueness. Its pullback is $\alpha$, since both maps agree after the etale atlas $W\to Y$. This proves descent of every morphism. The use of the limit test on $R_k$ does not require $R_k$ to be affine.

source.place: Tag 07SK, second paragraph: eventual equality on the kernel pair and descent to Y_k

proof.text: If two $T_i$-morphisms $a_i,b_i:Y_i\to Z_i$ have equal pullbacks to $T$, restrict them to an affine presentation $W_i\to Y_i$ as above. By the injectivity in [lem-sfb-lfp-space-scheme-limit-test], the resulting two maps $W_i\to Z_i$ agree after some base change to $T_j$. Since [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation] identifies $Y_j$ with the quotient $W_j/R_j$ of the base-changed atlas, their factorizations through it are then equal by the uniqueness clause of [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient]; hence $a_j=b_j$. Morphisms initially defined at different stages are first moved to a common stage by directedness. This proves precisely eventual equality of stage morphisms.

source.place: Tag 07SK, final paragraph: essential uniqueness, made explicit

proof.text: The explicit filtered $2$-colimit has objects represented at stages and morphisms represented by stage morphisms modulo eventual equality. The two preceding arguments make its Hom maps bijective, while the construction of $Y_i$ makes every object of $\mathsf{FP}(T)$ isomorphic to an image. To exhibit an inverse equivalence, choose for each $Y$ one such preimage and isomorphism; assign to a morphism the unique inverse image of its conjugate under these Hom bijections. Uniqueness makes identities and composition agree and gives the unit and counit isomorphisms. Thus the canonical functor is an equivalence, with exactly the three explicit clauses stated in the item. The chosen small index set and all these categories and colimits remain in the larger universe fixed by [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Tag 07SK, categorical reformulation of the proved object, morphism, and equality clauses
